reason: Under Example 6 the quote says s3:TlsVersion can be used in IAM, VPCE or bucket policies and to write policies that require a minimum TLS version; claim and displays match.
Under the Bucket policy heading the quote states wildcard characters on ARNs and other values grant permissions to a subset of objects; display is verbatim.
The quote states unpaginated ListBuckets is only supported at the default quota of 10,000 and accounts with an approved quota above 10,000 must paginate; claim and condition match.
Under Bucket quotas the quote states up to 10,000 general purpose buckets per AWS account by default and increases through the Service Quotas console.
The user guide quote gives the 10,000 default per account; the What's New quote (S3 item of 2024-11-14 in the feed) says any customer can request an increase up to 1 million buckets.
Under 'Additional information about all bucket types' the quote says you choose the Region at creation and cannot change the bucket name or Region afterwards.
The quotas table row Bucket tags has value 50, not adjustable, described as the maximum number of tags you can assign to an S3 bucket; per-bucket scope matches the description.
Under Use byte-range fetches the quote states concurrent connections fetch different byte ranges of one object for higher aggregate throughput and smaller ranges improve retry times on interruption.

The quotes say Bynder's access patterns change often (making traditional storage less cost effective) and Intelligent-Tiering reviews access patterns automatically, but neither states that Bynder chose Intelligent-Tiering because of this; the causal 'chose because' is inferred.
The quotes state Bynder allocates tags to each S3 bucket to track costs and adjust, and adopted AWS Cost Explorer to visualize, understand and manage costs and usage.
The quote states 18 PB, more than 175 million assets, stored in S3 Intelligent-Tiering, with storage cost savings of 65 percent; all displays verbatim.

Context says Snap began by analyzing access patterns; the quotes say Glacier Instant Retrieval would reduce costs as ideal for immediate-access data accessed once per quarter, and migration used S3 Lifecycle policies.
The quotes state more than 2 exabytes, roughly 1.5 trillion media files, migrated from S3 Standard-IA to Glacier Instant Retrieval, and tens of millions of dollars saved on storage as a result.

The announcement posted Mar 12, 2026 states buckets can be created in your own reserved namespace without globally unique names; the guide defines it as a subdivision only your account can create buckets in and gives the global default.

Document history (August 9, 2023) says Batch Operations Standard restores can start within minutes; the retrieval options note gives minutes/3-5 hours/1-2 PB per day for Flexible Retrieval and IT Archive Access; the What's New quote (same 2023-08-09 item) gives the previous 3-5 hours.
Document history dated April 27, 2023 states S3 automatically enables Block Public Access and disables ACLs for all new buckets in all Regions; FAQ and ownership page confirm both defaults.
The announcement posted Nov 26, 2025 states a policy attached at root or OU propagates to all sub-accounts in that scope and new member accounts inherit it; the guide lists the organization level.

The quotes give the current 10,000 default, a 2015 default of 100 and the 1 million request ceiling, but no quote states the date 2024-11-14 or that the default was raised from 100 to 10,000 on that date; the What's New sentence 'increased the default bucket quota from 100 to 10,000' is not quoted.
Document history dated September 30, 2024 states S3 now automatically approves bucket quota increases up to 1,000 buckets.

Document history dated September 16, 2025 states conditional deletes in general purpose buckets with if-match and an ETag, success only on ETag match, and s3:if-match in bucket policies to require the header on DeleteObject and DeleteObjects.

The quotes support conditional writes for PutObject and CompleteMultipartUpload dated August 20, 2024 and If-None-Match failing on an existing key, but the qualifier condition 'requests signed with Signature Version 4' is stated in no quote.

Two document history rows dated November 25, 2024 state the If-Match header fails the write on ETag mismatch and the s3:if-match and s3:if-none-match keys let bucket policies force clients to use the headers.
Document history dated December 1, 2024 adds CRC-64NVME; the integrity page says CRC64NVME is the default and AWS-owned clients send a checksum that S3 recalculates and validates before storing.

The default encryption FAQ quotes state that from January 5, 2023 all new uploads are encrypted at no additional cost and SSE-S3 applies to new buckets and existing buckets without default encryption.
Document history dated June 13, 2023 states DSSE-KMS applies two layers of encryption to objects when uploaded to S3.
The announcement posted Nov 19, 2025 states a default encryption setting enforcing SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS for all write requests and that PutBucketEncryption can disable SSE-C on specific buckets.

The announcement posted Jul 16, 2026 states system-generated tags in events to all destinations including EventBridge, SQS, SNS and Lambda, filterable across thousands of buckets with one EventBridge rule.
Document history dated November 28, 2023 describes S3 Express One Zone as a high-performance single-zone class for consistent single-digit millisecond access for latency-sensitive applications.
The announcement posted Apr 10, 2025 states reductions of 31% storage, 55% PUT, 85% GET and 60% per-GB upload and retrieval charges.
The announcement posted Jul 16, 2026 states transitions to Standard-IA and One Zone-IA as soon as 0 days after creation without the previous 30-day minimum retention in S3 Standard.

The announcement posted Apr 9, 2026 says Lifecycle no longer expires or transitions objects that failed replication; the guide says Lifecycle blocks actions on PENDING or FAILED objects and FAILED objects keep incurring storage costs.
Document history dated September 24, 2024 states the 128 KB default; the transitions page says an object size filter with ObjectSizeGreaterThan or ObjectSizeLessThan lets smaller objects transition.
Document history dated December 2, 2025 states 5 TB to 50 TB, multipart upload required, concurrent GetObject because a single GET is limited to 5 TB; the FAQ gives 5 GB for a single PUT.

Document history dated August 19, 2024 says unauthorized requests customers did not initiate are free; the billing note says AccessDenied 403 is not charged when initiated outside the owner's account or organization.

The availability page states that as of November 7th, 2025 Object Lambda is available only to existing customers and select APN partners; document history says it is no longer open to new customers from that date.
Document history dated November 20, 2023 says Object Lock can be enabled on an existing bucket; the configuration page says once enabled you cannot disable Object Lock or suspend versioning.
The announcement posted Sep 8, 2026 states an event hold with a retention duration protects the object while in place and S3 retains it for that duration after release.

Document history dated November 13, 2024 says RCPs set maximum available permissions on S3 buckets across the organization; the Organizations guide says no permissions are granted by an RCP, which sets limits.
Document history dated November 15, 2022 states restore requests up to 1,000 transactions per second per AWS account for Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive.
The announcement posted Apr 7, 2026 says S3 Files delivers a shared file system connecting any AWS compute to S3 data; the guide lists EC2, Lambda, EKS and ECS as mount targets.
